reviews.text:
As a generator installation company, we have used Invoice2go for over a year and have grown significantly during that time. While the platform itself has been helpful, we have encountered a major issue with payment processing limits.

Our business regularly invoices approximately $15,000 per generator installation, yet our monthly payout limit remains capped at $50,000. This means our funds are frequently held back, creating unnecessary cash flow challenges and forcing us to wait extended periods to access money that rightfully belongs to our business.

What has been most disappointing is the lack of resolution despite multiple attempts to address the issue. We have submitted requests to increase our payout limits, provided banking references, and even had our bank verify our financial standing and available funds across multiple accounts. Unfortunately, none of these efforts resulted in any meaningful action or communication.

For a growing business, reliable access to earned funds is critical. The inability to increase reasonable payout limits, combined with the lack of responsiveness, has been extremely frustrating and has negatively impacted our experience with the platform.

I hope Invoice2go will improve its support process and provide more flexibility for established businesses that have demonstrated a strong payment history and financial stability.

reviews.title: My Recent Experience With Invoice2go’s Payment System
reviews.text:
After more than a decade using Invoice2go to manage invoicing for my restoration business, I have always appreciated the platform for its practicality and ease of use. However, I recently encountered a situation that raised serious concerns about their new credit-card processing system and the quality of their customer support.

Invoice2go has recently resumed accepting credit-card payments through a third-party processor, Bill.com. Unfortunately, this change created unexpected complications that affected both me and my client. One of my customers did not recognize the charge from Bill.com on her American Express statement, and she disputed the transaction—even though the payment was legitimately made for services I provided.

Once I learned of the issue, I immediately clarified with my client that Bill.com was simply Invoice2go’s new processor. She confirmed the payment was valid and even sent a written statement explaining that she had authorized the charge. I forwarded her letter to Invoice2go, expecting a quick resolution.

Instead, the process became increasingly frustrating. Invoice2go refused to release the funds and requested an additional letter directly from my client’s American Express account—an unreasonable and inconvenient requirement for both my client and for me. Despite my effort to cooperate, I was eventually forced to obtain a copy of the original transaction directly from my client’s AMEX statement and send it to Invoice2go as further proof.

Even after providing that documentation, Invoice2go informed me that they would still hold the $3,600 payment for 90 days. The communication throughout the entire situation was slow, unclear, and extremely unhelpful. At no point did I feel supported as a long-standing customer who has trusted this platform for more than ten years.

A payment processor’s responsibility is not only to protect against fraud but also to support legitimate businesses when disputes arise. Holding funds for such an extended period—after the client confirms the legitimacy of the transaction—does not represent best practices. Combined with poor communication and unreasonable documentation demands, this experience has caused me to seriously reconsider whether Invoice2go’s current payment system is suitable for a professional business.

After years of loyalty, this was truly disappointing. I hope Invoice2go reviews these internal procedures and improves both transparency and customer service so that other small businesses do not face the same unnecessary inconvenience.

reviews.text:
If you’re considering Invoice2Go for your business, think again. Our experience with this company has been nothing short of a nightmare. In the middle of a busy business day, our account was suddenly locked, leaving us unable to invoice clients or access the money we had rightfully earned. This disrupted our operations entirely, causing unnecessary stress and financial loss.

Customer service was atrocious. There is no phone number to call, so we were forced to use their chat feature. Grace L., the first representative we contacted, was incredibly rude and unhelpful. She dismissed our concerns and told us to wait 24–48 hours for upper management to respond. As if we could just shut down our business and wait for them to figure it out—laughable! After Grace L. abruptly ended the chat, another representative tried to assist us, but the answer was the same: “Wait 24–48 hours.”

To make matters worse, they claimed our account was still accessible, which was a blatant lie. Not only could we not log in, but our employees were also locked out. The lack of accountability and transparency was appalling.

This company operates like a scam. They lock you out of your account, hold your funds hostage, and provide no immediate solutions. We have since closed our account and switched to Square, which has been far more reliable and professional.

Do yourself a favor and avoid Invoice2Go at all costs. Don’t risk your business with a company that clearly doesn’t understand how businesses operate.
Scam scam scam scam!

At this point, my hands are tied.  I finished a bunch of small jobs in the last two weeks and needed to get them billed out.  My business is small.  I typically have 1-2 service calls a day.  I am a sole proprietor and only employee.  I started using Invoice2Go many years ago when users were able to purchase the application (one-time).  Then, one day after an Apple update, the app disappeared.  You had switched to a cloud based platform in order to capitalize on annual fees and removed my ability to use the old software.  I understand the requirement to see continued revenue from those who continue to use your product.  Especially since you need to continue to update your software.  My problem is that your software, although it continues to evolve with additional features, does not align with what I need.  My business relies on many small jobs as a business model.  This means the need to write many invoices although the total revenue seen by the end of the year may is not the same as if I had multiple employees/users.  Because of this, I was able to stomach the $100/year fee that I was paying.  However, in order to continue to run my business in the same fashion as it always has, it appears I now need to pay 4 times that amount.  

As I had no time to mull over this decision, I was forced to purchase your premium plan.  That said, unless there are any pricing changes over the next year that consider businesses like mine, I will need to take my business elsewhere.
